topics.topic: Clock representations, precision, arithmetic, and rounding
questions: What exact type, unit and arithmetic representation stores monotonic readings and deadlines?
What exact type, unit and precision represents a monotonic reading used for session, confirmation and lockout deadlines?
What exact representations and precision does `clock` return for monotonic readings and UTC wall-clock instants, and how are duration additions and boundary comparisons rounded?

judgement.why: This is the same question previously judged about monotonic representation, precision, arithmetic and boundary preservation, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Monotonic instant representation and microsecond precision
quotes:
One reading in nanoseconds, comparable only with other readings of the same
process.

Every limit of A13 — 8 hours, 30, 15 and 10 minutes, 60 seconds — is
measured between two of these readings and never by the wall clock.
precedent.why: The later clock operation fixes monotonic readings as nanoseconds, which preserves the required microsecond distinction.

topics.topic: Owner-request monotonic sampling instant and reuse
questions: What event defines the request's arrival instant: receipt by the server, entry into the request handler, acquisition of a session-related lock, or the actual session check?
Does each owner request take one monotonic reading shared by session validity, the new last-request value and any confirmation-age check, or may those checks take separate readings?
Does each owner request take exactly one monotonic reading that is used both to check validity and to set `last_request`, and at what defined event is that reading taken?

judgement.why: The precedent already decides request-arrival sampling, reuse of the arrival reading, confirmation timing and the readings used by session operations, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Per-operation monotonic and wall-clock sampling and sharing
quotes:
- **Time.** An action has one instant: `operations` reads it from
  `clock.recorded_now` once, when the action's transaction begins, with
  today's date (`clock.today_in_utc`), and hands both to every module the
  action records a new instant or compares a date in. The import's records
  keep the instants their source holds ("Revisions and times"); the Customers
  it makes, its closure and its entry carry the action's one instant. The
  limits of A13 are read by `owner_sessions` from `clock.monotonic_reading`;
  the minute look of A18 rule 1 by `backups` from `clock.recorded_now`; a
  backup's instant is the one `store` reads at the read that fixes the
  copy's snapshot (A18 rule 1), which `backups` records and never reads
  itself; `instance_lifecycle` times its two passes by
  `clock.monotonic_reading`. No other module reads a clock.

A new owner session (M11) with its sign-in reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading`, no pending confirmation and no uploaded file; the
refusal count cleared. A refused sign-in outside a lockout counts at its
reading; the fifth less than 15 minutes old starts a 15-minute lockout.

At its arrival a request carrying a valid session restarts the session's
30 minutes, whatever its answer — a CSRF refusal included; of concurrent
arrivals the latest counts (A13 rule 2). A sign-out's admission marks the
session signed out at once.

The session's pending confirmation is replaced: a new value from
`random_values.make_secret_value`, bound to the action, its target, what the
step showed and the digest of its inputs in a fixed order, and the reading
of `clock.monotonic_reading` it was shown at.

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing.
precedent.why: The later module and public-operation texts assign one recorded action instant to every persisted fact and date comparison and separately fix the readings used by sign-in, request arrival, confirmation display and the expiry pass.

topics.topic: Security-review results after the latest A13 change
questions: What are the results of performing the security review again after the A13 change made since that latest review, at least for authentication_credential_abuse, browser_boundary and concurrency, which name A13?
Was the security review performed again after the A13 change now under review, and what are the resulting outcomes for every category that names A13?

quotes:
Performed again on 2026-11-11, after that day's changes to A01, A02, A04,
A07, A13, A15, A16, A17, A18 and A19 reopened it (rule 2): every category naming them —
injection_interpreted_input (A02, A16, A19), secrets, authentication and
concurrency (A01, A04, A07, A13, A15, A17, A18), browser_boundary (A13, A19),
files_artifacts (A07, A16, A18), authorization (A04) — was reviewed; the
changes to A01, A04 and A07 name constants and an exception of the
mapping's stage (4), and A07's concurrent publishes are those of different

topics.topic: Single UTC reading for audit-erasure validation and entry time
questions: Must validation of the supplied date, calculation of its UTC boundary and the erasure entry's instant use one UTC wall-clock reading, or may the operation read the wall clock more than once?
How many UTC wall-clock readings does an audit erasure take, and which reading defines both `today` for validation and the erasure entry's current instant when the operation crosses midnight?

judgement.why: The precedent decides that validation, today's date and the audit entry use the one UTC action instant sampled when the transaction begins.

precedent.topic: Whether erasure validation and audit creation share one UTC snapshot
quotes:
An operation that records an instant
  or compares a date takes the action's instant and today's date as inputs:
  `operations` reads the instant once with `clock.recorded_now` when the
  transaction begins and derives today from it with `clock.today_in_utc`
  ("Time"); the operation reads no clock.

`capability:store.run_in_transaction` opens the transaction with the
   instant and today's date from `capability:clock.recorded_now` and
   `capability:clock.today_in_utc`. `capability:audit_log.erase_audit_entries_before`
   refuses a date later than today and otherwise removes every entry whose
   instant is before 00:00 UTC of it (A15 rule 3).
precedent.why: State 5 requires one action instant at transaction start, derives today from that same instant, and passes the instant to the erasure entry.

topics.topic: Single shared UTC instant for all import records
questions: Is there one UTC import instant shared by every new Customer, the MigrationClosure and the import AuditEntry, and at what point in the transaction is it read?
What is the import's single instant, when is it read, and must that same UTC reading be used for every new Customer, the migration closure, and the import audit entry?

judgement.why: The precedent decides that every Customer made by the import, the closure and the audit entry share the single action instant read when the transaction begins.

precedent.topic: Definition and sharing of the single import instant across imported records, closure, and audit
quotes:
An action has one instant: `operations` reads it from
  `clock.recorded_now` once, when the action's transaction begins, with

precedent.why: State 3 explicitly makes the import's Customers, closure, and audit entry share the one action instant read when its transaction begins.

questions: When a correct sign-in creates a session, must its began and initial last-request instants use this pre-comparison reading, or may creation take a later monotonic reading after the credential comparison?

Must the one monotonic reading taken before credential comparison also become the successful session's `began`, `last_request`, and latest-expiry basis, or may session creation take another reading after comparison?

judgement.why: The precedent decides the number, timing and reuse of the sign-in attempt's monotonic reading, including the successful session's sign-in basis.

topics.topic: Whether files_artifacts must explicitly review A13
questions: Because the A13 change now decides when an expired session's uploaded file is retained and dropped, must files_artifacts be reopened and name A13, or is its reference to A16 considered sufficient evidence?

Must files_artifacts name and review A13 now that A13 decides that an expired session's uploaded import file remains until the next session pass, or is A16 intended to be the complete evidence for that lifetime despite delegating session ending to A13?

quotes: - files_artifacts: APPLICABLE; references: A07, A08, A16, A18, A19, A22; affected: M05, M10, import file, backups, pointers as references whose payload Registry never reads (R0-02)

An uploaded file is changed only by a holder of the import lock: an
   accepted import, holding it, drops every session's upload; the upload of
   a session ended by its limits goes with the session, when Registry ends it
   (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The files_artifacts references and A16's delegation of expired-session cleanup to A13 are unchanged from the closed text, and no reopening change made the omission of A13 newly material.

topics.topic: Cleanup-pass clock sampling and import-lock scope
questions: Does a pass take one monotonic reading for all sessions, or a new reading for each session after acquiring its lock, and is the import lock held across the entire pass or reacquired for each session?

judgement.why: The precedent quotes the later decision that the pass holds the import lock, takes one monotonic reading and decides every session by that shared reading under each session lock.

questions: Does reaching a time limit end and clear the session immediately, or merely make it invalid until the next 60-second pass ends and clears it?

quotes:
A session that has reached a
   limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check. Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.
judgement.why: The unchanged passage already distinguishes immediate invalidity from termination and cleanup at the next pass, and the reopening change did not touch or newly affect it.

questions: The passage must name this threshold as `the imported SIGN_IN_REFUSAL_LIMIT constant`, giving the decided value an explicit provider-constant path to generated code.

topics.topic: Handling admitted session-changing requests racing with termination
questions: If a confirmation, upload or other session-changing request passes the session check but the cleanup pass or sign-out acquires the locks first and ends the session, must the admitted request still succeed, must termination wait for it, or must it be rechecked and refused?

judgement.why: The precedent decides that an admitted request is not rechecked, completes while waiting, and is ordered ahead of the expiry pass or a later sign-out.

precedent.topic: Behavior when an admitted request races with session termination
quotes:
Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then: a session that has
reached 8 hours from sign-in or 30 minutes without a request, or is marked
signed out, serves no request; a change carries the CSRF value of its
session, compared in constant time (A13 rule 5). A request that passed
completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs or waits (A13
rule 2).

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing. Its turn on a session's lock comes after every change
of the session admitted before the pass began, which completes first with
the confirmation and the upload it may need (A13 rule 2).
precedent.why: State 5 says an admitted request is not rechecked and completes while waiting, and the expiry pass waits behind changes admitted before the pass began.

topics.topic: Session cleanup pass scheduling cadence and first run
questions: Is the pass scheduled at fixed monotonic deadlines from process start, 60 seconds after the preceding pass starts, or 60 seconds after it finishes, and when is the first pass?

topics.topic: Whether sign-in requires an existing owner session
questions: Is sign-in excluded from A09's term "owner action", so that it may be accepted without an existing owner session?

judgement.why: The precedent decides that sign-in is expressly exempt from the owner-session requirement and is checked only for the credential and lockout.

precedent.topic: Whether sign-in is an exception to the owner-session requirement
quotes:
Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session (sign-in
   excepted, A13 rule 4), then for a change its CSRF value (R0-29), then a confirmation value where one is
   asked (A13);

Sign-in is the one owner request made without a session:
   it is checked for the credential and the lockout only, carries no CSRF
   value, and the session cookie it sets is sent only to Registry's origin
   (rule 1).
precedent.why: A04 expressly names sign-in as the exception to the valid-owner-session check, and A13 defines the sessionless sign-in behavior.
